title: Founder MVP
outcome: Define a first product release as a founder: the vision, a bounded scope, the stories to build, the quality needs and the experiments to validate it.

minimumInputs.help: Who is the product for, and what should change for them?
minimumInputs.example: Small suppliers; they know when they will be paid without chasing.

minimumInputs.help: What is the idea, and what evidence or signals support it?
minimumInputs.example: Supplier status portal; we get twelve chase emails a week.

minimumInputs.help: What limits do you know about? Say "unknown" for anything you have not decided.
minimumInputs.example: Launch by spring; budget unknown.

minimumInputs.prompt: Idea or need in the user's words
minimumInputs.help: Describe the idea or the need the way you would explain it to a friend.
minimumInputs.example: Suppliers keep chasing us by email because they cannot see if their invoice was approved.

minimumInputs.help: What is in and out of scope for this exploration? Rough boundaries are fine.
minimumInputs.example: Invoice status only; payments and contracts are out of scope for now.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Anything not yet known about users, value or metrics is written as a hypothesis to test.
What need does this meet, or what outcome should it produce?
minimumInputs.example: Invoices approved within five days instead of nine.

minimumInputs.help: Name the solution or change, and where it starts and stops.
minimumInputs.example: An approval workflow in front of the finance system; the finance system itself is unchanged.

minimumInputs.help: What limits must be respected (budget, deadline, systems, rules)? Write "none known" if none.
minimumInputs.example: Must go live before the audit in March; cannot replace the finance system.

minimumInputs.help: Optional. Anything you already know is out of scope. Otherwise Kryterea proposes exclusions for you to confirm.
Who is the main user of what will be built?
minimumInputs.example: Approving managers who receive invoices for sign-off.

minimumInputs.help: What should the user be able to do that they cannot do today?
minimumInputs.example: Approve an invoice from their phone in under a minute.

minimumInputs.help: What is included in this piece of work, and what is not?
minimumInputs.example: Approval and rejection only; editing invoice details is not included.

minimumInputs.prompt: Acceptance expectations proposed where not confirmed
minimumInputs.help: Optional. How you would know a story is done. Kryterea proposes acceptance criteria where you have none, marked as proposed.
What does the solution cover, and where does it stop?
minimumInputs.example: The approval web app and its email notifications.

minimumInputs.help: Who uses it, what data does it handle, and where or when does it run?
minimumInputs.example: Around 40 managers, invoice and supplier data, used in office hours across two countries.

minimumInputs.help: Which qualities matter most, such as speed, security, availability or accessibility?
minimumInputs.example: Security of supplier bank details, and pages loading in under two seconds.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Any number you have not given (for example a response time) is proposed and marked for confirmation.
What do you believe is true but have not proven? Write it as a guess you can test.
minimumInputs.example: Suppliers who can see invoice status will stop emailing accounts payable.

minimumInputs.help: How could you test that guess quickly and cheaply? Or describe a test you already ran.
minimumInputs.example: Email ten suppliers a status link for two weeks and count follow-up emails.

minimumInputs.prompt: Distinguish planned work from observed results
minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Planned steps and real results are kept apart, so nothing is reported as done before it happened.
What question should the prototype answer?
minimumInputs.example: Can a manager approve an invoice on a phone without help?

minimumInputs.help: Who will try the prototype, and in what situation?
minimumInputs.example: A manager approving three invoices between meetings.

minimumInputs.help: What will the prototype include, and what will it fake or leave out?
minimumInputs.example: Clickable approval screens only; no real data or login.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Findings are only recorded from real test sessions, never assumed.
List the items you need to prioritise.
minimumInputs.example: Approval by email, mobile app, supplier portal, reporting dashboard.

minimumInputs.help: What goal should the priorities serve?
minimumInputs.example: Cut approval time in half within six months.

minimumInputs.help: How should items be ranked? Name criteria or a method, or say "suggest one".
minimumInputs.example: Value to the business versus effort; or suggest one.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Effort or value you have not estimated is left blank, never invented.

minimumInputs.prompt: Scope/requirements or explicit draft acceptance goals
minimumInputs.help: What will be tested? Paste the requirements, or describe what "working" means in your words.
minimumInputs.example: Managers can approve, reject and delegate invoices; approved invoices post to finance.

minimumInputs.help: Who will do the acceptance testing?
minimumInputs.example: Two approving managers and one accounts payable clerk.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Anything not yet known about the test environment is recorded as open.
